extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (responding to or drafting restriction/election actions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on making, responding to, and traversing restriction requirements and election-of-species matters in U.S. patent prosecution (MPEP/37 CFR-based rules and USPTO form paragraph changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Form Paragraphs (FPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the FPs apply to the instant application? Yes, if the application is filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), and plural inventions under 35 U.S.C. 121 are claimed. No, if the application is filed in the National stage under 35 U.S.C. 371. PCT unity of invention standards must be used for national stage entries. See MPEP 806.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FP changes published 1/21/10 apply to U.S. applications only; national stage (371) uses PCT unity standards and FPs do not apply. Compare claims to determine plural independent or distinct inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners must provide reasons and/or examples (MPEP 803)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Examiners must provide reasons and/or examples to support conclusions, but need not cite documents to support the restriction requirement in most cases."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner's statement of restriction cannot be a bare conclusion; supporting reasons or examples should accompany the requirement. (MPEP 803)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons must be concisely stated (MPEP 808)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The particular reasons relied on by the examiner for holding that the inventions as claimed are either independent or distinct should be concisely stated. A mere statement of conclusion is inadequate. The reasons upon which the conclusion is based should be given."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should provide concise, specific factual bases for independence/distinctness rather than conclusory language. (MPEP 808)

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction only if there is a serious search/examination burden
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examination and search of all the claims in an application can be made without serious burden, restriction should not be required, even though they are drawn to independent or distinct inventions, including species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If search/examination of all claims can be done without serious burden, the examiner must examine them on the merits. (1/21/10 memo; MPEP 803)

rubrics_metrics.name: Prima facie showing of burden
rubrics_metrics.description: "For purposes of the initial requirement, a serious burden on the examiner may be prima facie shown by appropriate explanation of separate classification, or separate status in the art, or a different field of search as defined in MPEP § 808.02. That prima facie showing may be rebutted by appropriate showings or evidence by the applicant."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner's initial requirement must articulate prima facie grounds (separate classification, separate status, different field of search); applicants may rebut with evidence or argument. (MPEP 803)

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush group exception (MPEP 803.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: "If the members of the Markush group are sufficiently few in number or so closely related that a search and examination of the entire claim can be made without serious burden, the examiner must examine all the members of the Markush group in the claim on the merits, even though they may be directed to independent and distinct inventions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Markush alternatives are few or closely related such that no serious burden exists, do not require provisional election of a single species. (MPEP 803.02)

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs 8.01, 8.02, 8.21 must specify at least one reason for burden
rubrics_metrics.description: To help ensure that all restriction requirements ... set forth the requisite burden, and to give applicants notice of why there is burden, form paragraphs 8.01, 8.02 and 8.21 have been revised to provide for the examiner to specify at least one applicable reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner notes list possible applicable reasons consistent with MPEP 808.02; the FP should insert the applicable reason(s) in the bracketed portion of the FP text. (1/21/10 memo)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reason A — Separate classification establishes burden
rubrics_metrics.description: "Separate classification thereof: This shows that each invention has attained recognition in the art as a separate subject for inventive effort, and also a separate field of search."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate classification indicates recognition in the art and a separate field of search; patents need not be cited to show separate classification. (MPEP 808.02)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reason B — Separate status in the art when classifiable together
rubrics_metrics.description: "A separate status in the art when they are classifiable together: ... each invention can be shown to have formed a separate subject for inventive effort when the examiner can show a recognition of separate inventive effort by inventors."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate status may be shown by citing patents as evidence of separate status and a separate field of search; applies even when classification is the same. (MPEP 808.02)

rubrics_metrics.name: Reason C — Different field of search
rubrics_metrics.description: "A different field of search: Where it is necessary to search for one of the inventions in a manner that is not likely to result in finding art pertinent to the other invention(s)..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: searching different classes/subclasses, different electronic resources, or employing different search queries/strategies. The different field of search must be pertinent to the subject matter covered by the claims. Patents need not be cited to show different fields of search. (MPEP 808.02)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use FP 8.01 when single-species claims present; FP 8.02 when only generic claims present
rubrics_metrics.description: "An examiner should set forth a requirement for election of a single disclosed species in a Markush-type claim — using form paragraph 8.01 when claims limited to species are present or — using form paragraph 8.02 when no species claims are present."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: where individual claims recite Compound X/Y/Z (use FP 8.01); where only generic or Markush claims are present (use FP 8.02). When both species and generic claims are present and election is warranted, use FP 8.01. (MPEP § 808.01(a); MPEP 803.02)

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of species requirement under 37 CFR 1.146
rubrics_metrics.description: "In the first action on an application containing a generic claim to a generic invention (genus) and claims to more than one patentably distinct species embraced thereby, the examiner may require the applicant in the reply to that action to elect a species ... However, if such application contains claims directed to more than a reasonable number of species, the examiner may require restriction of the claims to not more than a reasonable number of species before taking further action in the application."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must elect a species (or group of patentably indistinct species) in reply if required; examiner may limit number of species if more than a reasonable number are claimed. (37 CFR 1.146)

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of mutually exclusive species (MPEP 806.04(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: "Claims to different species are mutually exclusive if one claim recites limitations disclosed for a first species but not a second, while a second claim recites limitations disclosed only for the second species and not the first... to require restriction between claims limited to species, the claims must not overlap in scope."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mutually exclusive = non-overlapping claim scope in practice; use this test when determining whether restriction to a single species is proper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three types of 'species' that are not patentably distinct
rubrics_metrics.description: Species are not patentably distinct where: (1) the species are identical (scope identical); (2) the species overlap in scope (an embodiment in one anticipates an embodiment in another); (3) the species are distinct but would be obvious over each other under 35 U.S.C. 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If species are not patentably distinct for any of these reasons, election of a single species is improper; practice tips suggest electing the group of species and traversing the requirement using MPEP provisions. Examples in slides illustrate each type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressed admission of obviousness prevents restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: "If there is an express admission that the claimed inventions would have been obvious over each other within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. 103, restriction should not be required. In re Lee..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant's express admission that species are obvious variants undermines a restriction requirement; however, the admission may later be used by the examiner as a basis for an obviousness rejection of one species over prior art. (MPEP 803)

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner should group species considered unpatentable over each other
rubrics_metrics.description: "Election of species should not be required between claimed species that are considered clearly unpatentable over each other ... the examiner should group together species considered clearly unpatentable over each other."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If species are obvious variants (clearly unpatentable over each other), group them rather than require election; see MPEP 808.01(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Traversal and reconsideration procedures (37 CFR 1.143; 1.111(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant disagrees with the requirement for restriction, he may request reconsideration and withdrawal or modification of the requirement, giving the reasons therefor. In amending in reply to a rejection ... the applicant must clearly point out the patentable novelty ... and show how the amendments avoid such references or objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must present arguments/evidence in a traverse or in amendments; the examiner must reconsider and, if still maintaining the restriction, repeat and make it final, responding to the applicant's traverse. (37 CFR 1.143; 1.111(c); MPEP 821.01)

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific traversal grounds and burden-shifting (MPEP 806.05 subsections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific situations where applicant's proof/argument can shift the burden to the examiner include: combination/subcombination, subcombinations usable together, process and apparatus, process of making and product made, apparatus and product made, product and process of using.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant amends or proves that an asserted distinction is not material or an alternate use is not workable, the examiner must document another viable alternative or withdraw the restriction. Subsections: 806.05(c)-(h) provide the detailed tests and examiner obligations; practice tips advise precise facts/arguments to shift burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making a restriction requirement final after traverse (MPEP 821.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Where the initial requirement is traversed, it should be reconsidered. If, upon reconsideration, the examiner is still of the opinion that restriction is proper, it should be repeated and made final in the next Office action. ... In doing so, the examiner should reply to the reasons or arguments advanced by applicant in the traverse."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A repeated restriction after reconsideration should be made final, and must include a reply to the applicant's traverse. Finality procedures per MPEP 821.01 must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice tip: elect group of species and traverse when species are not distinct
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner requires an election between species that are not distinct (identical scope, single disclosed embodiment, overlapping breadth), Applicant may wish to elect the 'group of species' and traverse such a requirement using MPEP 806.03, 806.04(f) and 806.04(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided in the memo show claim sets and suggested traversals; electing a group preserves positions and triggers examiner reconsideration protocols.
